title: Pullback naturality of the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $X,Y$ be schemes of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p], let $u:X\to Y$ be a morphism, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the small pro-etale sites and constant coefficient sheaves $A_X,A_Y$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the derived module pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] with the canonical identification $u^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. For $T=X,Y$, let $F_T:T\to T$ be absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] and let
$$
\tau_T^{(b)}:L(F_T^b)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)},\qquad b\geq0,
$$
be the canonical trivialization induced by the relative Frobenius isomorphisms $r_{V/T}^{(b)}=(F_V^b,v):V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\times_{T,F_T^b}T$ for weakly etale objects $v:V\to T$: restriction along these isomorphisms identifies direct image by $F_T^b$ with the identity, the adjoint identification gives the inverse-image trivialization of module sheaves (the coefficient identification being that of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]), and the inverse image being exact, it induces $\tau_T^{(b)}$ termwise on complexes. For $b=1$ this specifies the canonical trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]; $\tau_T^{(0)}$ is the identity.

Using the canonical composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], the equality $uF_X^b=F_Y^bu$ gives the pullback-composition identification
$$
 c_{u,b}:Lu^*L(F_Y^b)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(F_X^b)^*Lu^*.
$$
As natural transformations on $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ one has
$$
 (\tau_X^{(b)}Lu^*)\circ c_{u,b}=Lu^*\tau_Y^{(b)}.
$$
Moreover, for integers $b_1,b_2\geq0$ and $T=X,Y$, the trivialization $\tau_T^{(b_1+b_2)}$ equals the composite
$$
 L(F_T^{b_1+b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(F_T^{b_1})^*L(F_T^{b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\tau_T^{(b_1)}L(F_T^{b_2})^*}L(F_T^{b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\tau_T^{(b_2)}}\operatorname{id},
$$
whose first arrow is the composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $F_T^{b_1+b_2}=F_T^{b_2}\circ F_T^{b_1}$; in particular $\tau_T^{(b)}$ is the $b$-fold iterate of $\tau_T^{(1)}$.

proof.text: Use the normalized witnesses r, comp and tau of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], including their projection, conjugate-section and unit-section equations. Retain its addition and exponent-zero clauses; only its open-restriction clause must be strengthened to arbitrary scheme morphisms.

For a scheme morphism u in characteristic p, prove naturality of each iterated absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. The underlying maps are identities; on sections the assertion is map_pow. This supplies w : F_X^b u = u F_Y^b.

Using base change [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], compare the relative-Frobenius maps on B_u V under the two pullback-composition isomorphisms. Equality into the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] is checked on its projections. The first projection follows from the normalization of r and Frobenius naturality in step 2; the second is the structure-map equation. Invert this equality of isomorphisms to obtain the equality of maps used by contravariant restriction.

Pass to direct images of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Mathlib unit_conjugateEquiv identifies the conjugate of tau with its unit-section formula. Transport the section normalization of comp along w by equality induction. On each module, site object and section, the two composite direct-image maps are equal by presheaf functoriality applied to step 3. Apply injectivity of Mathlib conjugateEquiv, its composition and whiskering formulae and its unitor formulae to deduce the ordinary inverse-image naturality square.

Apply the exact termwise derived functor to the ordinary square. The proved source-library mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_trans, mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_symm and whiskering/composition/unitor coherence equations in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.MapDerivedCategoryMate transport this equality to the specified derived comparison. Equality induction identifies the derived image of eqToIso w with eqToHom of the induced functor equality. This is exactly the required arbitrary-pullback clause. Combine it with the retained witnesses, addition law and zero normalization from step 1.
